modelAnswer: NUCLEI AND STRUCTURES: (1) Facial nucleus → muscles of facial expression, stapedius, stylohyoid, posterior belly of digastric; (2) Nucleus ambiguus → stylopharyngeus (IX), pharyngeal and laryngeal muscles (X), sternocleidomastoid and trapezius (XI); (3) Dorsal motor nucleus of X → parasympathetic to thoracic and abdominal viscera; (4) Hypoglossal nucleus → intrinsic and extrinsic tongue muscles.

COLUMNS OF CRANIAL NERVE NUCLEI: (1) Somatic Efferent (III, IV, VI, XII) → voluntary muscles of eye and tongue; (2) Special Visceral Efferent (V, VII, IX, X, XI) → muscles of pharyngeal arch origin (mastication, facial expression, swallowing, phonation); (3) General Visceral Efferent (III, VII, IX, X) → parasympathetic to glands and smooth muscle; (4) Visceral Afferent (VII, IX, X) → taste and visceral sensation.

COLUMN FUNCTIONS: (1) Somatic Efferent → voluntary eye and tongue movement; (2) Special Visceral Efferent → mastication, facial expression, swallowing, speech; (3) General Visceral Efferent → pupil constriction, lacrimation, salivation, digestion, heart rate; (4) General/Special Visceral Afferent → taste, visceral pain, baroreception.

NUCLEI AND FUNCTIONS: (1) Hypoglossal nucleus → controls tongue movement and shape; (2) Nucleus ambiguus → swallowing, phonation, gag reflex; (3) Dorsal motor nucleus of X → parasympathetic regulation of heart, lungs, GI tract; (4) Vestibular nuclei → balance, equilibrium, eye-head coordination; (5) Cochlear nuclei → auditory processing and hearing.
